summary: Streaming JSON-mode responses causing sporadic long-tail decode delays and client timeouts
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reports intermittent 30s+ request times and client-side timeouts when using structured output (JSON-mode) with streaming=true on dedicated capacity. Impact:
- Several checkout microservices experienced prolonged latency spikes during peak traffic (10:45-11:20 UTC).
- Errors are request timeouts (client sees 504) and occasional server-side 5xx.
Environment:
- Dedicated cluster: dc-dedicated-42 (us-east)
- Redwood runtime v2.7.3, api-gateway v1.4.1
- Customers are pinned to model redwood/openchat-7b-v1 with structured-json output template
Steps to reproduce:
1) Create a generation request with streaming=true and mode=json_schema with template producing ~15KB structured payload per request.
2) Fire concurrent 250 RPS from BrightCart test harness for 10 minutes.
3) Observe tail latency and errors from client side after ~5 minutes.
Observed behavior:
- Median latency is normal (~120ms) but 99.9th percentile spikes to 20-45s.
- Traces show long delays in "serialize_and_flush" spans and large CPU time in worker processes handling JSON encoding.
Expected behavior:
- Streaming JSON responses should not cause long-tail serialization delays; flushes should be constant and under SLOs.
Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Suggested reducing streaming buffer flush interval and switching streaming=false (non-streaming) for now; customer applied non-streaming and errors subsided.
comments: Support (2026-03-10) - Maya Chen: Customer reported spikes after enabling structured JSON mode with streaming=true. Asked for request IDs and sample payloads. Requested authorization to pull traces and CPU profiles from their dedicated pool.

Customer (2026-03-10) - Aaron Patel (BrightCart): Sent request IDs sup_req_9831..9839 and sample prompt+schema. Noted spikes correspond to peak traffic window and only for JSON-mode; plain text mode unaffected.

SRE (2026-03-11) - Diego Ramos: Pulled flamegraphs for worker processes on dc-dedicated-42. Observed synchronous JSON encoding calls that pinned a worker thread for large outputs. Opening investigation into serialization backpressure and streaming flush logic.

Engineering (2026-03-11) - Lina Park: Reproduced locally with load generator. Confirmed that when structured outputs exceed ~8KB and streaming enabled, the runtime batches and then performs blocking encoding on main worker leading to increased per-request tail latency.

Support (2026-03-12) - Maya Chen: Notified customer that we identified a likely serialization/backpressure issue and are testing a hotfix that performs async encoding off the critical I/O path. Provided ETA for patch rollout.
Customer (2026-03-12) - Aaron Patel: Thanks team; will keep non-streaming enabled until fix is rolled. Requested follow-up monitoring when hotfix is live.
investigation_notes: 03/11 - Collected pprof CPU profiles from three workers on node rwi-dc-42-worker-5. Top stack shows runtime.serializeJSON -> encoding/json.Marshal -> internalBuffer.Write blocking for 300-800ms per request at tail.

03/11 - Trace capture (trace IDs provided) shows serialize_and_flush spans accumulating in queue; backpressure appears when more than ~200 concurrent streaming frames are pending for a single worker process.

03/11 - Reproduced with load harness: switching to streaming=false keeps tail latency below 500ms. Enabling streaming + structured template reproduces 99.9th percentiles > 20s within 5 minutes at 250 RPS.

03/11 - Hypothesis: JSON-mode triggers use of full in-memory encoding for structured outputs; combined with streaming frame aggregation, large outputs cause blocking CPU work on hot threads instead of being offloaded to async workers. This creates head-of-line blocking and increases long-tail latency.

03/12 - Correlated incident with recent change in v2.7.3 that modified streaming flush coalescing and buffer threshold (PR 1168). That change increased per-frame aggregation to improve throughput but unintentionally increased worst-case encoding chunk sizes.

03/12 - Identified quick mitigation: reduce coalescing buffer threshold on dedicated clusters to avoid huge encoding work in single operation. Prepared a hotfix branch that also offloads serialization to a separate goroutine pool.

03/12 - Added observability tasks: instrument per-request serialization_time_ms, frames_coalesced_count, and cpu_ms_per_serialize. These metrics will be emitted to console and customer dashboards for affected clusters.
03/12 - Linked to PR for patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1189 (adds async-serialization and config flag streaming.coalesce_max_bytes)
03/12 - Follow-ups: schedule config rollout for dedicated clusters, add safety limit on coalescing, add integration test for streaming+structured outputs to ci-load tests.
resolution: Workaround applied: customer switched to streaming=false which restored normal latency. Engineering prepared hotfix (PR 1189) that: (1) reduces default streaming coalescing threshold to 8KB on dedicated clusters, (2) offloads JSON serialization to an async worker pool to avoid blocking main serving thread, and (3) emits per-request serialization telemetry. Hotfix deployed to canary on dc-dedicated-42 on 2026-03-12 22:10 UTC, observed 99.9th latency drop from 28s->380ms under reproduction load. Plan: roll to remaining dedicated clusters on 2026-03-13 during maintenance window. Post-deploy actions: update runbook, add CI test coverage, notify customers of config option streaming.coalesce_max_bytes and guidance for schema size.
